problem: Existing social navigation benchmarks and methods only assess path efficiency and pedestrian collision avoidance, ignoring language-instructed social rules and scene semantics. VLM/VLA navigation agents are too slow (seconds per inference, <1 Hz) for dynamic crowds.
motivation: Robots in human environments such as hospitals or warehouses must follow instructions (follow a doctor, avoid restricted zones, hurry vs. be careful) while avoiding moving people in real time. Direct VLM action generation loses dynamic targets due to latency, so slow semantic reasoning must be decoupled from fast reactive control.
key_idea: Use a slow VLM agent (with perception tools) to modulate the inputs (semantic costmap layer) and parameters (SFM weights) of a classical fast social-force controller, instead of having the VLM output actions.
insight: Semantic markers projected into the costmap are updated by LiDAR at the fast-loop rate, so the semantic targets stay tracked between the ~7 s VLM calls. This explains the Follow Doctor task, where the method gets 100% SR while both direct-VLM baselines get 0% and lose the target due to latency. The baselines also lack segmentation tools, which hurts region-avoidance (Region Score 80.50 vs 43.28/36.56). The paper has no ablations, so the evidence is comparative and from the latency table.
method: Slow VLM reasoning agent: GPT-4o receives the first-person RGB image, instruction and history about every 10 s and calls tools to output SFM parameters and visual markers
Perception tools: RoboPoint provides navigation goal points and Grounded-SAM 2 segments persons/regions (doctor, door, traffic line) to be projected into the costmap

Parameter updater: the system prompt predefines mode-specific values (e.g. Follow: sfm_people_weight 2.0, sfm_goal_weight 0.5; Goal: goal weight 1.0; idle: velocities near 0), applied via update_sfm_param

Fast SFM local planner: sum of desired, obstacle, social and group forces, run at ~5 ms/step; for the doctor the social force is replaced by short-range repulsion plus long-range attraction (following band [d_min,d_max])
Dynamic SocialLayer costmap: VLM-assigned base cost, inflation radius and decay give an exponential potential field C(d)=C_base e^{-λd} around segmented entities, merged with other layers by max

LISN-Bench: Arena 3.0 (ROS/Gazebo) with region masks, pedestrian identities/meshes and precomputed trajectories; 5 tasks (hospital, warehouse) covering pedestrian following/avoidance and region reaching/avoidance; metrics SR, collision rate, path smoothness, subject score, region score

setting.backbone: GPT-4o (frozen) with RoboPoint and Grounded-SAM 2 as tools, plus a classical SFM controller
setting.observation: egocentric RGB + LiDAR scan, plus language instruction
setting.action_space: continuous differential-drive velocity (v, ω) from the SFM controller

results: Social-Nav-Modulator reaches 100/100/90/100/66.67% SR on the five tasks (abstract: 91.3% average), while VLM-Nav and VLM-Social-Nav mostly stay below 60% and both get 0% on Follow Doctor. It also has lower collision rates in most tasks and much better Region Score in Forklift Carefully (80.50 vs 43.28/36.56).
limitations: Simulation-only evaluation with a small task set (5 tasks, 5-9 repeats per scenario) and no real-robot validation
The VLM loop is slow (~7 s per call, slower than VLM-Social-Nav's 1.75 s) and mode-parameter rules are hand-predefined in the prompt
Only two baselines, no ablations, and social norms limited to zone/distance rules
builds_on: Social Force Model (HuNavSim SFM local controller)
